curriculum.lesson_evidence: Archaeology studies material remains of the past. An artefact is a human-made object; its meaning depends on find context (where and with what it was found). Ethical practice includes legal protection of sites and not disturbing or removing artefacts illegally.
curriculum.scope_limit: Proposed Stage 4 NESA HSIE alignment using catalogue outcome code HT4-1; content-point mapping remains pending. Local First Nations protocols and Community verification remain pending human review. Do not invent Country names, Dreaming stories, sacred knowledge or unverified cultural claims.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Explain why context matters for one artefact type and list two ethical rules for sites.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: Context links object to place/layer; ethics include no unauthorised digging/removal and reporting finds.

WATCH FOR
Treating archaeology as treasure hunting. The goal is understanding, not collecting souvenirs.
